prompt.context: Our client is called Meditest – they make equipment for blood sample test labs. Specifically, their machines are used to test blood samples for their glucose levels, meaning they are used to monitor diabetes. Their machines are very expensive, often costing more than $20K, and they must be operated by professionals. They also make the consumables that go in these machines. Meditest has a presence only in Europe. The market for these large machines is growing very slowly and Meditest is looking for more growth. They have designed patient-operated machines that can do simple glucose level tests. These devices are small and portable, are easy to operate, and do not need much in the way of extra consumables.
prompt.question: Meditest is considering launching this device, called glucore, in the UK. They have retained McKinsey to examine what considerations they should have in this launch.

clarifying_info.q: What is the population of the UK?
What share of the UK population is over 65?
clarifying_info.a: 20% of the population is over 65 years old

clarifying_info.q: What percentage of people over 65 have diabetes?
clarifying_info.a: 5% of those over 65 are currently diabetes sufferers

clarifying_info.q: What percentage of people under 65 have diabetes?
clarifying_info.a: 1% of the population under 65 are currently diabetes sufferers

clarifying_info.q: What share of diabetics will buy the device each year?
clarifying_info.a: 10% of the diabetic population buys glucore every year

clarifying_info.q: What is the price of the glucore device?
clarifying_info.a: 120 pounds today; expected to fall 50% to 60 pounds in 4 years

clarifying_info.q: How will the diabetic population grow?
clarifying_info.a: The total diabetic market will grow by 33% in 4 years (from ~1.08M to ~1.44M people)

clarifying_info.q: What market share does Meditest expect in 4 years?

framework: Internal considerations: capabilities (can Meditest manufacture/distribute a consumer product?), capital (funding required for launch), culture (shift from B2B professional to B2C consumer)
External considerations: competition (existing consumer glucose monitors), regulation (UK medical device approval, NHS), market trends (diabetes prevalence growth, technology cost curves)
Customers: market size (number of diabetics in the UK), segmentation (by age/severity), preferences (convenience, ease of use), payment assistance (NHS coverage, insurance co-pay)
Why UK?: why not other geographies, why not other value-added services for the core professional product line

questions.prompt: How large is the market for glucore in the UK today (in number of people)?
questions.guidance: Candidate should segment the UK population by age, apply diabetes prevalence rates to each segment, then apply the annual purchase rate. Key steps: (1) split 60M into over-65 (12M) and under-65 (48M); (2) apply 5% and 1% diabetes rates; (3) sum to get total diabetics; (4) apply 10% annual purchase rate.

math.setup: UK population = 60M. Over-65 = 20% * 60M = 12M. Under-65 = 80% * 60M = 48M. Diabetics over-65 = 5% * 12M. Diabetics under-65 = 1% * 48M. Annual buyers = 10% of total diabetics.

questions.prompt: What will revenues be in 4 years given projected price, market growth, and market share?
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply the 33% market growth to get new diabetic population, recalculate annual buyers at 10%, apply 25% market share, then multiply by the new price (50% lower). Candidate should also reflect on whether 2.16M pounds is a meaningful revenue target for a company that sells machines at 20K+ each.

math.setup: In 4 years: diabetic population grows 33% to ~1.44M. Annual buyers = 10% * 1.44M = 144K. Meditest market share = 25%. Price = 120 * 50% = 60 pounds.
steps: New diabetic population: 1.08M * 1.33 = ~1.44M (or stated as 144K buyers total market)
math.answer: 2.16 million pounds per year in 4 years

questions.prompt: How does 2.16M pounds sound, and what levers could Meditest pull to increase revenues?
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognise that 2.16M pounds is very small relative to a company selling 20K machines. Key levers: expand geographically beyond UK, grow market share, slow price erosion, target additional customer segments (e.g. pre-diabetics), bundle with consumables or services.

questions.prompt: How would you think about pricing the glucore device?
questions.guidance: Candidate should anchor value to the consumer: convenience (no need to visit a physician), time savings, and money savings. Should recognise that in the UK many consumers do not directly pay for physician visits (NHS), so the direct savings argument is weaker. Insurance/NHS co-pay model is relevant — insurers benefit from better glucose monitoring because it reduces catastrophic events (hospitalisations, complications), so they may be willing to subsidise the device.

brainstorming.prompt: What levers could Meditest pull to increase the revenue potential of the glucore launch?

categories.name: Market expansion
ideas: Launch in additional European countries beyond the UK
Target markets with higher diabetes prevalence or less existing competition
Consider markets without universal healthcare where consumer willingness-to-pay is higher

categories.name: Market share
ideas: Differentiate on brand trust (Meditest's professional heritage)
Position as the most convenient or most accurate consumer device
Partner with NHS or private insurers to be the recommended device

categories.name: Pricing and monetisation
ideas: Slow price erosion through product innovation and feature differentiation
Introduce a subscription or consumables model (test strips, services)
Explore insurance reimbursement or co-pay programmes to sustain effective price

categories.name: Customer base
ideas: Target pre-diabetics or at-risk populations beyond confirmed diabetics
Expand to other glucose-monitoring use cases (athletes, diet management)
Leverage professional customer relationships to drive consumer referrals

recommendation: A UK launch of glucore is strategically reasonable given Meditest's existing European presence and diabetes market expertise, but the standalone UK revenue opportunity (2.16M pounds in 4 years) is small relative to Meditest's current business and investment required

To make the launch worthwhile, Meditest should treat the UK as a beachhead and plan a rapid multi-country European rollout, pursue insurance/NHS co-pay partnerships to sustain pricing, and leverage its professional brand to gain consumer trust
risks: Revenue ceiling is very low if launch remains UK-only with price falling 50% in 4 years
Competition from established consumer glucose monitor brands (e.g. Abbott, Roche) could limit market share gains
Regulatory approval timelines in the UK (MHRA) could delay launch
Consumer adoption may be slower than projected if NHS covers physician visits at low or zero cost to patients
next_steps: Assess regulatory pathway and timeline for MHRA approval of glucore as a consumer device
Map competitive landscape for consumer glucose monitors already sold in the UK
Model multi-country European rollout to size the broader revenue opportunity
Engage NHS and private insurers to explore co-pay or reimbursement programmes
